content.overview: Culpable homicide (s. 100) is the genus; murder (s. 101) is the species. Punishments are s. 103 (murder) and s. 105 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder). IPC 302 is BNS 103, not 101. s. 106(2) is not in force.

content.study:
Topic at a glance
[[REF:CONCEPT:CRIMINAL-LAW:CULPABLE-HOMICIDE]] is the most marked homicide question in Indian criminal law. The BNS keeps the Govinda architecture and changes the numbers.

What the law says
s. 100 — culpable homicide: causing death with intention of causing death, or intention of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death, or knowledge that the act is likely to cause death.
s. 101 — when culpable homicide is murder: the four classic clauses (intention to cause death; intention of injury known to be likely to cause death of the person; intention of injury sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death; knowledge that the act is so imminently dangerous that it must in all probability cause death).
s. 103 — punishment for murder (death or imprisonment for life, and fine). s. 103(2) is the five-or-more-person murder (lynching) clause.
s. 105 — punishment when the killing is culpable homicide not amounting to murder (exceptions to s. 101, or the residual s. 100 cases).
s. 106 — death by rash or negligent act. s. 106(2) (hit-and-run causing death and fleeing) is not in force.

Why the distinction exists
Not every killing with a guilty mind is murder. The law grades intention and knowledge. Provocation, private defence exceeded in good faith, sudden fight, and consent (the exceptions) drop murder to s. 105. They do not acquit.

Essential elements
1. Death of a human being.
2. Caused by an act of the accused.
3. The mental element in s. 100 (intention or knowledge of likely death).
4. Then ask: do the s. 101 clauses fit? If yes, is an exception made out? If no exception, s. 103. If exception or only s. 100 knowledge, s. 105. If only rashness/negligence without that knowledge, s. 106.

How courts read the clauses
Regina v. Govinda still teaches the difference between “likely” (s. 100) and “sufficient in the ordinary course of nature” (s. 101 third clause). Virsa Singh: once the bodily injury intended is made out, and that injury is sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death, murder is complete — the accused need not have wanted death as such.

Current-law position
Offences on or after 1 July 2024: BNS numbers. Before that date: IPC 299/300/302/304/304A (s. 358 + Article 20(1)). Do not write 302 as the current punishment section.

Educational note
Reuse the canonical concept; this page is the exam expansion.

provisions.title: Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder

examples.title: Example 1 — simple
examples.body: A, in a sudden quarrel, strikes B once with a stick on the arm. B later dies of an unexpected clot. Intention to cause death is not made out; even “injury sufficient in the ordinary course” may fail. This is the classic “likely / sufficient” problem — often s. 105 or even less, depending on knowledge.

examples.title: Example 2 — legal
examples.body: Five persons, acting together, beat a man to death in public because of a rumour. s. 103(2) is the lynching clause. Common intention ([[REF:DOCTRINE:CRIMINAL-LAW:COMMON-INTENTION]] s. 3(5)) may also apply, but 103(2) does not require the 3(5) prior-concert test in the same way. Unlawful assembly / common object (s. 190) is a third, distinct route.

hypotheticals.question: Murder or culpable homicide not amounting to murder?
hypotheticals.analysis: The chest stab in the ordinary course is sufficient to cause death — the third clause of s. 101 is prima facie murder. The live question is the provocation exception. If the provocation was grave and sudden and A had not cooled down, the killing drops to s. 105. It does not become an accident or a rash act (s. 106).

rows.left: Intention or knowledge that death is likely
rows.right: The four murder clauses — a higher quality of intention/knowledge

rows.left: The residual and the excepted killings
rows.right: If an exception applies, it is no longer punished as murder

misconceptions.trap: BNS 101 is the punishment for murder.
misconceptions.correction: 101 is the definition. Punishment is s. 103. IPC 302 maps to 103, not 101.

misconceptions.trap: BNS 304 is culpable homicide not amounting to murder.
misconceptions.correction: BNS 304 is snatching. CHNAM punishment is s. 105 (old IPC 304).
The Sanhita commenced on 1 July 2024 except s. 106(2).

questionsAndAnswers.question: State the BNS sections for definition and punishment of murder.
What happens when an exception to s. 101 is made out?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: The killing is culpable homicide not amounting to murder, punished under s. 105 — not an acquittal.

cases.name: Regina v. Govinda
cases.holding: The difference between culpable homicide and murder turns on the degree of likelihood and the nature of the intended injury.
cases.relevance: Still the teaching case for the clauses. Apply BNS 100/101 numbers.

cases.name: Virsa Singh v. State of Punjab
cases.holding: If the accused intended the bodily injury, and that injury is sufficient in the ordinary course of nature to cause death, the third murder clause is satisfied even if death as such was not desired.
cases.relevance: Foundational locus classicus on third clause of murder.

cases.name: State of A.P. v. Rayavarapu Punnayya
cases.holding: Culpable homicide is the genus, murder the species. Always start with s. 100 (old 299) before climbing to murder.
cases.relevance: Opening sentence of a good homicide answer.

examFrameworks.question: Distinguish culpable homicide and murder under the BNS.
steps: Govinda / Virsa Singh in one principle each.
Exceptions drop to s. 105; they do not acquit.

examFrameworks.question: Explain the scheme of homicide in Chapter VI BNS with exceptions and punishments.
steps: Four clauses of s. 101 with Virsa Singh on the third.
IPC concordance and date of offence.

revisionPoints: 100 definition CH; 101 definition murder; 103 punishment murder; 105 CHNAM.
examTips: If the facts are a mob killing, mention 103(2) and then, separately, 3(5) / 190.
